required_content.problem: Once unrestricted model weights are published, the original releaser generally cannot recall copies, enforce serving-layer safeguards, observe use, or prevent derivatives. This irreversible transition has different control semantics from theft prevention and restricted custody. A model card, default refusal behavior, license, checksum, takedown request, or pre-release benchmark cannot control post-release fine-tuning, redistribution, merging, quantization, hidden deployment, or cumulative ecosystem effects.
required_content.core_mechanism: An open-weight release should require a prospective irreversible-release case that binds the exact artifact and license to accessible-frontier comparison, malicious-fine-tuning and scaffolded elicitation, marginal and cumulative risk, benefit and access distribution, downstream safeguard portability, derivative lineage, incident channels, post-release measurement, and residual ownership; after release, governance may inform, patch, coordinate, and support safer derivatives, but it must not claim revocation authority it no longer possesses. Classify access tiers and make the irreversible transition from custody to public replication explicit.
required_content.worked_trace: Create an irreversible-release dossier for a harmless small model. Freeze exact bytes and comparators; test default and deliberately safety-removed variants; record license, documentation, signatures, derivative metadata, incident channels, patch semantics, and the limits of recall. Use the exercise to verify decision records, not to authorize release of a hazardous model. Evaluate the exact candidate, competent maliciously fine-tuned variants, strong scaffolds, and the current accessible frontier under matched budgets. Assess marginal risk, cumulative ecosystem risk, expected benefits, access distribution, and who bears residual harm.
required_content.failure_boundary: default-model-only evaluation weak malicious fine-tuning stale accessible-frontier comparator license-as-control illusion
required_content.evidence_state: This chapter remains Design rationale at argument support. Its contracts, examples, tests, or local artifacts establish only their encoded scope. A finite open-weight decision may hand off only when artifact identity, irreversibility, comparator, fine-tuning state, residual owner, and post-release non-authority are explicit; no theorem authorizes release. Default alignment is never treated as a safeguard that determined downstream users cannot remove. Post-release actions are not described as recall, revocation, or complete containment.
required_content.non_claims: No chapter claim or evidence state is promoted by this visual. A named mechanism is not proof of correct implementation or useful deployment. A local check or formal model does not establish real-world enforcement. No safety, transfer, state-of-the-art, AGI, or ASI conclusion follows.
